P1.evidence: Read back the setter work — 'I went through everything that you and Kim chatted about already, plus your application, so I already have a pretty solid head start on you.' Full four-part frame delivered verbatim in structure: 'where you are today, where you want to go, what's been getting in the way, and then what you genuinely need to get there.' Frame agreement asked ('Does that all work?', diarization put it on the prospect's line) and answered 'Oh, yeah, definitely.' Open question ran clean: 'What could we potentially help you with today?'

P2.evidence: Ran the baseline almost completely and in order: 'can you walk me through your age, height, weight, please?'; 'What do you do for work right now?' followed by 'I would imagine that's mostly sitting during the day'; 'Any health conditions?'; 'Do you have any injuries or chronic pain, anything that limits your movement?'; 'how many times a week?'; 'what are you hoping to get from Kettlebell specifically that you're not getting from these other things?'; 'What's your diet look like?' with a good follow-up on eat-out frequency; 'How are your energy levels day to day?'. Sleep is the one gap — the rep never asked, the prospect volunteered it ('the only problem is the sleep... I need way less sleep than I used to normally need') and the rep closed it out with 'Yeah, could be both. Could be both' rather than probing. Scored a miss per the volunteered-information rule.

P3.evidence: Aesthetics/function asked directly — 'if you could change one thing about your body, what would it be?' — and the menu question ran ('Whether that's like mobility energy'). The why-bridge ran twice and worked: 'what's the reasoning behind that? Like, why do we actually want to build the strength?' and 'what is all this leading towards, man?', which surfaced dating, self-actualisation and confidence. But the rep never asked what he physically wants to do and can't, never asked who else this impacts (no family, friends or legacy stakeholder was ever brought into the room), and never reflected the deep goal back for confirmation — instead he outsourced the summary: 'if we had to kind of summarize all of that in a sentence... how would we summarize that all in a sentence, I guess?' The prospect then rambled for four minutes about manifestation and the rep let it run. Drive-through to identity happened ('a more actualized version of my full potential') but was prospect-led, not rep-led.

P4.evidence: The past-attempts material arrived unprompted inside the opening monologue (college gym phase, walking streak that lapsed) rather than from a scripted 'what have you tried before / what happened with that' — credit is partial on that basis. The one thing in the way was asked properly and twice: 'what's held you back from getting out and actually starting it?' The prospect named the gap himself — gym access and habit formation — and the rep reflected it: 'barrier of entry kind of thing.' The root-cause move was never run: no 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own?', and the rep let the answer stay at logistics ('if I could just do it in my apartment') without testing whether a kettlebell at home actually fixes a consistency problem the prospect has failed at three times.

P5.evidence: The consequence frame was inverted into an aspiration frame. The rep ran 'let's say it's two years down the road, or even six months down the road, and you're looking in the mirror and you see that fully actualized version of Michael, like, what do you see?' — the positive vision, never 'if nothing changes.' No cost of inaction, no 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not', no line in the sand. This is the phase carrying 20 weight and it did not run at all. It also cost him the leverage: the prospect is a manifestation-and-abundance thinker who will happily talk about the upside for ten minutes, and without the downside frame the call had no tension when the clock ran out.

P6.evidence: No belief question ('do you believe you can actually get there with the right structure and the right person in your corner?'). The all-in test ran in a soft, leading variant: 'it feels like something that where it's like, hey, we are really wanting to go all in on something right now. Is that what I'm understanding?' — answered yes but immediately qualified by the prospect with the real risk ('if I'm all-in on everything, do I have enough time to be all-in on everything?'), which the rep did not close down. P6c is N/A because nothing was presented on this call.

P11.evidence: No close attempted. The call ended in a rebook, not a payment step: 'we'll pop on right around that time and I'll break down everything, man.'

notes: Textbook opening and near-complete baseline, then the call drifted: 51 of 59 minutes went to discovery and the rep let a highly verbose prospect run long stretches unmanaged, so consequence frame and commitment check never happened and the offer was pushed into a second call. Coach the clock — the hard stop was disclosable at minute one and the rep only asked about cutoffs at 00:51. Two live signals were also left on the table: the prospect said he'd only want one-on-one 'a couple months to get the motions down' and that he is already inside Primal University, both of which need answering before price, not after.
